findings.message: The conversions preserve addresses using ALIGN_TYPE, whose documented contract requires pointer capacity. ULONG remains port-specific and the existing ULONG helpers remain unchanged. Alignment and guard reservations retain existing behavior for valid supplied stacks; no new overflow issue was found. The casts match SMP creation and explicitly document the MISRA deviation; formal MISRA compliance is not established.

The behavioral regression tests use independent remainder arithmetic, require actual high-address storage, and check metadata, size, fill boundaries, padding and creation state. The original tree documents 64 failed metadata assertions across 16 MISRA cases and four safe scheduling failures; its control passes. The frozen candidate passes all six tests, including host-suite discovery.

Current verification is prepared-with-baseline-failure, not fully passing. SMP has one failed randomized preemption-threshold assertion among 590 tests. The unchanged baseline independently fails the same assertion with matching image, configuration, affinity and normalized compile/link commands. This supports draft preparation only; upstream final-head SMP CI remains mandatory. Single-core has 807 passing tests; the explicitly qualified FreeRTOS profile has three.

Historical failures remain separate. Default affinity 0,1,2,3 and disabled-notification assertions reproduce on baseline. Historical trace affinity 0,1,2,3 passes all ten baseline attempts, so exact-affinity equivalence is unproven; paired trace failures establish only affinity 0,2,4,6. The historical event-flag timeout also lacks baseline reproduction after ten attempts and has unavailable exact candidate command comparison. None of these failed suites is relabeled passed.

findings.message: Scheduling tests exercise genuine Linux creation, sleep/wake and completion, while execution stacks remain pthread-owned. They establish simulator metadata and scheduling behavior, not execution on the supplied hardware stack. Unavailable target execution, reference-toolchain checks and formal MISRA analysis remain unavailable.
